# Skills For Real Engineers [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/mattpocock/skills)](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy. If you want to keep up with changes to these skills, and any new ones I create, you can join ~60,000 other devs on my newsletter: [Sign Up To The Newsletter](https://www.aihero.dev/s/skills-newsletter) ## Installation (30-second setup) A plugin updates itself. [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) copies editable files into your project, and you update them by hand. Pick one per agent, because installing both gives you every skill twice. ### 1. Get the skills
Claude Code ```bash claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official ``` Updates itself by default.
Codex ```bash codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Updates itself at startup.
GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code) ```bash copilot plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills copilot plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Then, once, add to `~/.copilot/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "mattpocock": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "mattpocock/skills" }, "autoUpdate": true } } } ``` In VS Code, run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source** and enter `https://github.com/mattpocock/skills`. It updates daily.
Gemini CLI (manual updates) ```bash gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/engineering gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/productivity ``` Re-run both commands to update.
Any other agent, or editable files (manual updates) ```bash npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a # cursor, opencode, devin, windsurf, amp, pi; omit -a to choose ``` When the installer asks which skills to take, include `setup-matt-pocock-skills`. To update, run `npx skills@latest update`, and re-run `add` to pick up new skills.
### 2. Run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` In your agent, run it once per repo. It will: - Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, GitLab, local files, or anything else you describe) - Ask you what labels you apply to tickets when you triage them (`/triage` uses labels) - Ask you where you want to save any docs we create ### 3. Bam - you're ready to go. ## Why These Skills Exist I built these skills as a way to fix common failure modes I see with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents. ### #1: The Agent Didn't Do What I Want > "No-one knows exactly what they want" > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**. The most common failure mode in software development is misalignment. You think the dev knows what you want. Then you see what they've built - and you realize it didn't understand you at all. This is just the same in the AI age. There is a communication gap between you and the agent. The fix for this is a **grilling session** - getting the agent to ask you detailed questions about what you're building. **The Fix** is to use: - [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md) - for non-code uses - [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md) - same as [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md), but adds more goodies (see below) These are my most popular skills. They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them _every_ time you want to make a change. ### #2: The Agent Is Way Too Verbose > With a ubiquitous language, conversations among developers and expressions of the code are all derived from the same domain model. > > Eric Evans, [Domain-Driven-Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Domain-Driven-Design-Tackling-Complexity-Software/dp/0321125215) **The Problem**: At the start of a project, devs and the people they're building the software for (the domain experts) are usually speaking different languages. I felt the same tension with my agents. Agents are usually dropped into a project and asked to figure out the jargon as they go. So they use 20 words where 1 will do. **The Fix** for this is a shared language. It's a document that helps agents decode the jargon used in the project.
Example Here's an example [glossary](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/blob/076a5a7a182db0fe1e62971dd7a68bcadf010f1c/CONTEXT.md) (still named `CONTEXT.md` at that pinned commit, from before the skills renamed the convention), from my `course-video-manager` repo. Which one is easier to read? - **BEFORE**: "There's a problem when a lesson inside a section of a course is made 'real' (i.e. given a spot in the file system)" - **AFTER**: "There's a problem with the materialization cascade" This concision pays off session after session.
This is built into [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md). It's a grilling session, but that helps you build a shared language with the AI, and document hard-to-explain decisions in ADR's. It's hard to explain how powerful this is. It might be the single coolest technique in this repo. Try it, and see. > [!TIP] > A shared language has many other benefits than reducing verbosity: > > - **Variables, functions and files are named consistently**, using the shared language > - As a result, the **codebase is easier to navigate** for the agent > - The agent also **spends fewer tokens on thinking**, because it has access to a more concise language ### #3: The Code Doesn't Work > "Always take small, deliberate steps. The rate of feedback is your speed limit. Never take on a task that’s too big." > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**: Let's say that you and the agent are aligned on what to build. What happens when the agent _still_ produces crap? It's time to look at your feedback loops. Without feedback on how the code it produces actually runs, the agent will be flying blind. **The Fix**: You need the usual tranche of feedback loops: static types, browser access, and automated tests. For automated tests, a red-green-refactor loop is critical. This is where the agent writes a failing test first, then fixes the test. This helps give the agent a consistent level of feedback that results in far better code. I've built a **[`/tdd`](./skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md) skill** you can slot into any project. It encourages red-green-refactor and gives the agent plenty of guidance on what makes good and bad tests. For debugging, I've also built a **[`/diagnosing-bugs`](./skills/engineering/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md)** skill that wraps best debugging practices into a disciplined loop, gated phase by phase. ### #4: We Built A Ball Of Mud > "Invest in the design of the system _every day_." > > Kent Beck, [Extreme Programming Explained](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Extreme-Programming-Explained-Embrace-Change/dp/0321278658) > "The best modules are deep. They allow a lot of functionality to be accessed through a simple interface." > > John Ousterhout, [A Philosophy Of Software Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Philosophy-Software-Design-2nd/dp/173210221X) **The Problem**: Most apps built with agents are complex and hard to change. Because agents can radically speed up coding, they also accelerate software entropy. Codebases get more complex at an unprecedented rate. **The Fix** for this is a radical new approach to AI-powered development: caring about the design of the code. This is built in to every layer of these skills: - [`/to-spec`](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md) quizzes you about which modules you're touching before creating a spec And crucially, [`/improve-codebase-architecture`](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md) surveys a codebase for deepening opportunities and hands you the candidates. I recommend running it on your codebase once every few days. It is a survey, not a rescue: on a genuinely old codebase it will find real candidates, but it won't untangle the mud for you. ### Summary Software engineering fundamentals matter more than ever. These skills are my best effort at condensing these fundamentals into repeatable practices, to help you ship the best apps of your career. Enjoy. ## Reference These split on one axis: who can invoke them. **User-invoked** skills are reachable only when you type them (e.g. `/grill-me`); their job is to orchestrate. **Model-invoked** skills can be invoked by you _or_ reached for automatically by the agent when the task fits; they hold the reusable discipline. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, but never another user-invoked one. ### Engineering Skills I use daily for code work. **User-invoked** - **[ask-matt](./skills/engineering/ask-matt/SKILL.md)**: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the user-invoked skills in this repo. - **[grill-with-docs](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md)**: Grilling session that also builds your project's domain model, sharpening terminology and updating `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs inline. - **[triage](./skills/engineering/triage/SKILL.md)**: Move issues through a state machine of triage roles. - **[improve-codebase-architecture](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md)**: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick. - **[setup-matt-pocock-skills](./skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md)**: Configure this repo for the engineering skills (issue tracker, triage labels, domain doc layout). Run once per repo before using the other engineering skills. - **[to-spec](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md)**: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker. No interview, just synthesizes what you've already discussed. - **[to-tickets](./skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md)**: Break any plan, spec, or conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, written as text in a local file, or as native blocking links on a real tracker. - **[implement](./skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md)**: Build the work described by a spec or set of tickets, driving `/tdd` at pre-agreed seams and closing out with `/code-review` before committing. - **[implement-spec](./skills/engineering/implement-spec/SKILL.md)**: Implement a whole spec on one integration branch. # security-audit

A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in [Build your own vulnerability harness](https://blog.cloudflare.com/build-your-own-vulnerability-harness). The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

## What it does

The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

1. **Reconnaissance** -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in `architecture.md` and `coverage-ledger.json`.
2. **Coverage-led hunting** -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.
3. **Candidate validation** -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.
4. **Structured output** -- write `confirmed`, `needs_validation`, and `rejected` records to `findings.json` and validate them against `report-schema.json`.
5. **Independent record verification** -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.
6. **Target-neutral reporting** -- derive `REPORT.md`, `FINDINGS-DETAIL.md`, and `NEEDS-VALIDATION.md` from the verified records and coverage ledger.

The parent runs `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs `validate-findings.cjs` in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

The verdicts are distinct: `confirmed` has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, `needs_validation` has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and `rejected` records a disproved candidate.

Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `SKILL.md` | Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns |
| `RECONNAISSANCE.md` | Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions |
| `HUNTING.md` | Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules |
| `ATTACK-CLASSES.md` | Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts |
| `MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md` | Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets |
| `AI-AND-LLM.md` | Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets |
| `WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md` | HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets |
| `CLIENT-SIDE.md` | DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets |
| `SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md` | Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes |
| `CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md` | IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes |
| `PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md` | RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes |
| `RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md` | Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes |
| `DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md` | Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes |
| `DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md` | Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes |
| `VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md` | Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting |
| `report-schema.json` | JSON schema for all three `findings.json` verdicts |
| `validate-findings.cjs` | Zero-dependency validator for `findings.json` in Phases 4 and 5 |
| `validate-findings.test.cjs` | Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks |
| `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` | Zero-dependency validator for `coverage-ledger.json` in Phases 1–5 |
| `validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs` | Coverage-ledger validator tests |

## Installation

Install the skill with the [Skills CLI](https://skills.sh):

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
  --skill security-audit
```

Use `--global` for a user-level installation:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
  --skill security-audit \
  --global
```

Run `npx skills --help` for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

## Usage

Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

```
security audit this codebase
```

```
find security vulnerabilities in ./src
```

```
do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project
```

The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to `~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N>`. The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

## Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents
- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators
- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as `needs_validation` instead of executing target code.

## Design principles

- **Only confirm established boundary failures.** Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as `needs_validation` with its exact unresolved fact.
- **Adversarial validation.** The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.
- **Severity requires impact.** Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.
- **Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities.** If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.
- **Multiple runs improve coverage.** In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

## Contact

Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

## License

details.readme:
# rea-video Reverse-engineer any video. Talking-head, tabletop, AI video, 3D, motion graphics, mixed edits: give it any of them,
and it tells you shot by shot how the visuals, styled text, editing and audio were made, then gives you a plan to make one yourself. [中文](i18n/README_zh.md) | English | [Русский](i18n/README_ru.md) | [日本語](i18n/README_ja.md) | [한국어](i18n/README_ko.md) | [Español](i18n/README_es.md) | [Português](i18n/README_pt.md) | [Français](i18n/README_fr.md) | [Deutsch](i18n/README_de.md) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/JuneYaooo/rea-video?style=flat)](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video/stargazers) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-%E2%89%A53.10-blue) ![Agent](https://img.shields.io/badge/runs%20in-Claude%20Code%20%7C%20Codex-8A2BE2) Left: a TikTok ad shot on a phone. Right: someone's AI remake with a different product swapped in.
rea-video's verdict: the left is all live footage, one set and two camera positions; the right is all AI-generated, and its 8 shots can be produced in 3 generations.
> Reports come out in the language you ask in (Chinese or English; your agent passes `--lang`). The detailed docs are in Chinese for now; your agent reads them and answers in your language. The six example reports below are in English, so you can see what a report looks like without installing anything. ## What it can break down | Video type | Examples | What you get | |---|---|---| | Live footage | Talking-head, tabletop, handheld product demo, vlog, store visit | Setups and camera positions, framing, camera moves, lighting (12 setups with gear lists), color grade | | AI video | Text/image-to-video, AI short drama, AI music video | Evidence, a reverse-engineered prompt per shot, how to batch into generations and which model to use | | Avatar | A portrait driven by audio, lip-sync | Which shots are avatar shots, what portrait and audio you need | | 3D / animation | Blender / C4D explainers, product animation, 2D animation, stop-motion | Whether to generate with a video model or render from 3D code | | Code / template | Kinetic type, UI demos, charts, slide-style cards | Text, layout and motion timing, ready to rebuild as a Remotion project | | Screen recording | Software tutorials, web demos | Which parts are real material you'll need to record yourself | | Mixed / edits | AI characters + code UI + real screen capture; live footage with AI edits | Each shot judged separately, then reassembled on the original timeline | Besides how the picture was made, every video also gets: - Captions and styled text: start and end of each line (exports to SRT / ASS), plus color, outline and how the text comes in - Stickers, emoji, picture-in-picture: where they sit and how long they stay - Editing: where the cuts are, how fast, whether they hit the beat - Audio: human or AI voice, AI or library music and its BPM, where each sound effect lands - Material you'll supply yourself: screen recordings, screenshots, product photos ## Quick start rea-video is built for AI agents. In Claude Code, Codex or any agent that can run commands, say: ```text Install https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video, then break down this video: /path/to/video.mp4 ``` The agent installs the CLI, learns the workflow and runs the whole thing. You need ffmpeg and Python 3.10+.
Install by hand ```bash brew install ffmpeg # or: sudo apt install ffmpeg git clone https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video && cd rea-video bash scripts/install_skill.sh # installs the CLI (pip, or pipx / a local .venv if pip is blocked) and links the skill into ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.agents rea-video --help ```
You get: - a one-line summary, e.g. "41% AI video + 59% code UI, 8 s of real screen recording, library music at 122 BPM" - a remake plan, split into what to film, what to generate and what to code - a full `report.html` with per-shot frames, evidence, prompts, camera and lighting notes, and the audio breakdown Add a video-capable model — Gemini or Doubao both work: give the agent the endpoint and key. It makes live/AI/3D calls more accurate and writes a reverse-engineered prompt for every shot. Without one it still works; if your agent can see images, it will check the uncertain shots itself. ## Examples The sample videos in `docs/cases/videos/` are re-compressed to keep the repo small, which strips the TikTok / Douyin platform tags. Running them yourself gives different results from the reports below, especially without a vision model. Use the original platform download to reproduce.

Mixed-media clip · 19 s · 10 shots
AI characters talking + code-built UI + 8 s of real screen recording. The 5 dialogue shots are split up by UI segments but share one set, so one generation covers them.
Video · Report
3D explainer · 67 s · 21 shots
All 3D, AI narration. Doable as 10 video generations, or have an LLM write Blender / Three.js code.
Video · Report

Product promo · 70 s · 12 shots
83% code-driven motion graphics, 12% screen recording. No video model needed; one Remotion project does it.
Video · Report
AI music video · 165 s · 86 shots
Correctly flags the song as AI-generated (it was made with Suno). The vision model called some shots "live-action drama"; the agent spotted fake Chinese characters on a scroll and ruled them AI.
Video · Report

Live-action unboxing · 72 s · 29 shots
All real footage: an overhead phone rig, one rug, one camera position, no voice-over, room sound plus library BGM. After platform transcoding the offline tool called 35% of it AI; agent review brought it to 97% live-action.
Video · Report
AI + real person hybrid · 58 s · 21 shots
75% real (talking head + filming a phone screen) and 25% AI: the creator fed her own on-camera clip and two product photos to Jimeng to generate a "real-person" product segment. The AI part was caught by the Jimeng watermark and garbled text on the gift box.
Video · Report
## Remakes After rea-video breaks a video down, the remake recipe in [capsule-cinema](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/capsule-cinema) generates a new version: camera, motion, pacing and transitions follow the original, only the elements you choose are swapped. These results were generated with a self-hosted MiniMax H3: the original shot is the motion reference, and keyframes with the swapped elements (gpt-image-2) set the look. Below are three remakes that OiiOii showed in its WeChat articles. For each we made two versions: the same swap as OiiOii, and one that also swaps the subject, setting and props. Each GIF plays four versions in sync: original, OiiOii remake, our remake, element-swap version.
Overhead outfit change · 12 s
Same swap: woman → man, three outfits → matching menswear. Element swap: a girl in three historical Hanfu outfits in a Chinese study; the remote becomes a round fan.

HD comparison video (with audio) · same-moment stills
Paper-craft / watercolor animation · 30 s
Same swap: new clay girl as the lead. Element swap: a fox; forest → coral reef, clouds → starry sky, sunset → aurora.

HD comparison video (with audio) · same-moment stills
Handheld product video · 21 s · 11 shots
Same swap: an original new product, English sticker → Chinese caption. Element swap: pink product, kitchen → camping table, new ingredients.

HD comparison video (with audio) · same-moment stills
The HD comparison videos use the original audio. The originals and OiiOii versions come from the articles and are shown for comparison only. ## Accuracy How-it-was-made accuracy, weighted by shot duration: | | Tuning set (15) | Holdout (16) | Re-encoded WeChat videos (10) | |---|---|---|---| | Tools only (offline, free) | 98.3% | 99.6% / 98.9% | 88.6% | | + vision model (Gemini) | — | 99.6% / 99.8% | 99.6% | | + agent visual review | — | 99.6% / 99.8% | 100% | The two holdout numbers are holdout (9 videos) and holdout2 (7 videos). On original files the tools alone are mostly enough. Videos downloaded from platforms have been recompressed, which wipes out the noise evidence, so it takes a vision check to get back above 99%. Real-asset detection is 97–99%, and shot boundaries are all correct. Numbers and how to reproduce them: [eval/RESULTS.md](eval/RESULTS.md). ## How it works ![rea-video pipeline](docs/rea-flow_en.svg) 1. Split: cut the video into shots and separate audio into voice, music and effects. 2. Gather evidence: measure the frames (frame cadence, sensor noise, whether the whole image is panning as one plane, AIGC tags in metadata); look at the images (hands, text, physics); listen (BPM, key, singing vs speech). 3. Decide: hard evidence like AIGC tags and frame cadence outranks "looks like". Conflicts are flagged for the agent to review visually. 4. Plan the remake: batch shots according to what the target video model can actually do, such as max clip length, multi-shot support and how many reference images it takes. ## FAQ
How is this different from one-click remake tools like Hypit? [Hypit](https://github.com/hypit-ai/hypit) takes a reference video and makes a new one: the agent reads frame grids to understand the original, generates footage with the models it supports (Seedance, PixVerse, MiniMax, Wan and others), and renders captions and motion graphics in HTML. It doesn't ask how the original was made. A live-action source goes through the same pipeline; it won't tell you how many cameras were used or how it was lit. What AI video it can match depends on the models it has: no Kling or Veo, and no dedicated avatar or 3D path, and no AI music: you bring your own. # Horizon **Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, rewritten in Rust.** Your worlds, the same rules and the same terrain as the Java game, checked against it by hundreds of differential tests, in one native program with no Java. Free, open source (MIT) and unofficial: you play it with your own copy of Java Edition.

## What works today Everything below is in the current release. - **The game.** Survival, creative, hardcore and spectator; vanilla world generation in all three dimensions, mobs, villagers, raids, redstone, every command, the HUD and the recipe book. Vanilla saves open as they are, and worlds from 1.8 to 26.2 are upgraded. - **Multiplayer.** Join vanilla and Horizon servers (online mode included), open a world to LAN, or invite friends with a code from the launcher's Home page. - **Graphics.** Distant terrain up to 1,024 chunks, graphics presets, HDR and controllers, all off by default where they would change the vanilla look ([settings](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/settings)). - **Packs.** Resource packs, data packs and shader packs ([below](#mods-and-shader-packs)). - **Mods.** Content mods and native Rust mods, installed from the launcher ([below](#mods-and-shader-packs)). - **Servers.** Host one from the launcher, or run `horizon-server` on a VPS ([below](#host-a-server)). - **The launcher.** It installs and updates the game, prepares its files from your copy of Minecraft, and updates itself.
Nightly 2026-11-05 on a Mac mini (Apple M4 Pro, Metal): vanilla's textures, no mods or shader packs, render distance 32 with distant terrain on. ## Download Get **the Horizon launcher** from [playhorizon.dev](https://playhorizon.dev), or from [the launcher releases](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/releases?q=launcher&expanded=true): | Platform | File | Needs | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows x64 | `horizon-launcher-setup.exe` | Windows 10 or 11, a GPU with Vulkan or DirectX 12 | | Windows on Arm | `horizon-launcher-setup-arm64.exe` | Windows 11 on Arm | | macOS, Apple Silicon | `horizon-launcher-macos-arm64.dmg` | macOS 12 or later | | macOS, Intel | `horizon-launcher-macos-x64.dmg` | macOS 12 or later | | Linux x86-64 | `horizon-launcher-linux-x86_64.AppImage` or `.tar.gz` | a glibc distribution, X11 or Wayland, a GPU with Vulkan or OpenGL 3.3 | **You also need a Microsoft account that owns Minecraft: Java Edition.** You sign in with it in the launcher, which plays only with an account that owns the game ([why](docs/microsoft-account.md)). Horizon contains no Minecraft code or assets: an existing install (official launcher, Prism, MultiMC...) is reused, and without one the launcher downloads 26.3 from Mojang for your account. Step by step: [Install and first launch](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/install).
## Mods and shader packs - **Content mods** (`.hmod`): blocks, items, recipes, loot, models and textures, with no code. - **Native mods** (`.hnmod`): Rust that the launcher compiles into the game for you, with nothing to install. - **Java mods** (Fabric, NeoForge, Forge) don't run: Horizon has no Java. The launcher carries over the data and assets inside their jars, and imports modpacks (`.mrpack`, CurseForge zips, Prism instances) the same way ([modpacks](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/modpacks)). - **Shader packs**: Iris/OptiFine-format packs (`shaders/` folders) and Horizon's own WGSL packs, under Video Settings → Shader Packs ([pack format](docs/shaders.md)). Mods are off by default: a fresh install plays exactly like vanilla 26.3. The launcher's Mods page browses Horizon's registry and Modrinth. [Mods](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/mods) · [make a mod](docs/mods.md). ## Host a server The launcher's **Servers** page creates, starts, backs up and updates a server, and invites friends. On a VPS, `horizon-server` installs with one command, needs no Java, and takes vanilla 26.3 and Horizon players alike. [Host a server](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/hosting) ([reference](docs/hosting.md)). ## Agent control AI agents and scripts can play Horizon. `horizon-ctl`, shipped with the game, reads its state as JSON and acts like a player; `horizon-ctl mcp` serves the same commands over MCP. ```sh horizon-ctl launch --world Survival --seed 5 --wait # finds the version the launcher installed horizon-ctl state # position, health, food, target, screen... horizon-ctl goto -0.5 65 -2.5 --near 2.5 # walks there along a path horizon-ctl break -1 65 -3 # mines it; replies with the drops ``` `horizon-ctl help` lists every command. [Agent control](docs/native-client.md#agent-control-horizon-ctl-and-mcp). ## Build from source Needs Rust 1.90+, Python 3.10+, JDK 25, and on Linux `libasound2-dev libudev-dev`. `horizon-prepare` builds the game's resources from **your own copy** of Java Edition 26.3 (checked against `research-lock.json`) and never downloads it: 1. **Client:** play 26.3 once in the official launcher. Horizon reads `~/.minecraft` (or `--minecraft-dir` / `HORIZON_MINECRAFT_DIR`). 2. **Server jar:** the 26.3 server jar (`downloads.server.url` in `versions/26.3/26.3.json`), passed once with `--server-jar` or `HORIZON_SERVER_JAR`. ```sh git clone https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon.git cd horizon cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- --prepare --server-jar ~/Downloads/server.jar # needs JDK 25 cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- sounds # optional: sounds from your launcher install cargo run --release -p horizon-client ``` Prepared files land in the gitignored `.local/`: never commit or share them. Options, controls and architecture: [the native client guide](docs/native-client.md); all developer docs: [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome: read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) (vanilla first, small pull requests), and see [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) or [playhorizon.dev/hub](https://playhorizon.dev/hub) for what's next. Questions: [Discord](https://discord.gg/playhorizon). Before a pull request, run the self-check and paste its output: ```sh git config core.hooksPath .githooks python3 tools/pr_ready.py ``` It runs rustfmt, clippy, the touched crates' tests, the Python tests, the public-tree check and the vanilla harnesses your change affects. Never commit game files, decompiled source or prepared resources. ## Project status **Player-visible gaps: 0 open** of the 833 the [port ledger](tools/port_ledger.py) found, reading every vanilla 26.3 method against Horizon's code: vanilla behaviour a player would notice that Horizon doesn't have yet. By area: Animals [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3512); Monsters and bosses [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3513); Entities, projectiles, vehicles and decorations [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3514); Items, enchantments and inventories [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3515); Blocks, redstone and fluids [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3516); World, world generation and saves [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3517); Screens, HUD and client packets [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3518); Entity and block rendering, models [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3519); Server and players on the server [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3520); Mob AI, villagers and raids [0](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3521). This number goes down as gaps close (`tools/parity_gaps.py`); the harness results below say that what is tested matches. The table is the project's own audit: every subsystem matches vanilla in every harness that compares it. 100% means 100% of what the harnesses compare, not that nothing else differs. What players still run into: [known issues](docs/known-issues.md). ### Java parity: 100% Scores: 0 (absent), 0.25 (started), 0.5 (playable, major features missing), 0.75 (mostly complete) or 1 (complete and verified by differential tests); the percentage is their average. Last audited 2026-10-13: the harnesses pass on Linux and macOS. HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/studio-app) is free to use as well; its [Pro plan](https://hyperframes.studio/pricing) adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes`, `/reverse-any-video`, `/style-sampling` and `/figma` install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 9 skills. details.readme:
# d2-web **Play Diablo II: Lord of Destruction in your browser.** The 1.13c engine, reimplemented and compiled to WebAssembly, by [Virtastic](https://virtastic.app).

▶ Play now at diablo2.virtastic.app · Website · Discord · YouTube · Issues

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join%20the%20server-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/PzFfDkbSue) [![Support on Patreon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Patreon-support-F96854?logo=patreon&logoColor=white)](https://www.patreon.com/virtastic) [![Support on Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ko--fi-buy%20us%20a%20coffee-FF5E5B?logo=ko-fi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/virtastic) [![YouTube](https://img.shields.io/badge/YouTube-Virtastic-FF0000?logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/@Virtastic-Apps) [![Reddit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Reddit-r%2Fvirtastic-FF4500?logo=reddit&logoColor=white)](https://www.reddit.com/r/virtastic) ![License: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blue) ![Platform: Chrome desktop](https://img.shields.io/badge/browser-Chrome%20%2F%20Chromium-brightgreen) An unofficial reimplementation of the Diablo II: Lord of Destruction **1.13c** engine, compiled to **WebAssembly** and played in the browser. No game data is included: you bring your own legally owned copy. > **Status: playable.** Create a character and play: towns, wilderness and dungeons, combat and > skills, items, vendors, waypoints and saves, in a browser tab with nothing to install. Some > details still differ from the original game. If you find one, please > [report it](https://github.com/Virtastic/d2-web/issues). ## Contents - [Before you start](#before-you-start) - [Choose how to play](#choose-how-to-play) - [Option A: Play in your browser](#option-a-play-in-your-browser) - [Option B: Run your own server with Docker](#option-b-run-your-own-server-with-docker) - [Option C: Build from source](#option-c-build-from-source) - [Option D: Desktop app](#option-d-desktop-app) - [Play on other devices on your network](#play-on-other-devices-on-your-network) - [Widescreen menu backgrounds (optional)](#widescreen-menu-backgrounds-optional) - [Build and publish your own Docker image](#build-and-publish-your-own-docker-image) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [Tests](#tests) · [Layout](#layout) · [Contributing](#contributing) · [Credits](#credits) · [Legal](#legal) ## Before you start You need two things: 1. **Your own copy of Diablo II and Lord of Destruction**, installed on your computer. d2-web ships **no Blizzard files**: no art, sound, text, maps or programs. It reads them from your install. 2. **A desktop Chrome, Edge or other Chromium browser.** The game files are the `.mpq` files in the folder Diablo II is installed in: | file | what it holds | |---|---| | `d2data.mpq` | the world: maps, monsters, items | | `d2exp.mpq` | Lord of Destruction | | `d2char.mpq` | the heroes | | `d2sfx.mpq` | sound effects | | `d2speech.mpq`, `d2xtalk.mpq` | speech | | `d2music.mpq`, `d2xmusic.mpq` | music | | `d2video.mpq`, `d2xvideo.mpq` | cinematics | | `patch_d2.mpq` | the patch | > [!TIP] > **Where is my Diablo II folder?** It is the folder that holds `d2data.mpq`. It is usually > `C:\Program Files (x86)\Diablo II` on Windows and `/Applications/Diablo II` on macOS. From > WSL2, the Windows folder is `/mnt/c/Program Files (x86)/Diablo II`. ## Choose how to play | | you need | best for | |---|---|---| | **[A. Play in your browser](#option-a-play-in-your-browser)** | a browser | just playing | | **[B. Run your own server with Docker](#option-b-run-your-own-server-with-docker)** | Docker | hosting it yourself, at home or on a server | | **[C. Build from source](#option-c-build-from-source)** | Docker, Node.js 24+, git, and a game **patched to 1.13c** | changing the code | ## Option A: Play in your browser 1. Open **** in Chrome. 2. Click **CHOOSE FOLDER** and pick your Diablo II folder. You can also click **CHOOSE FILES**, or drag the `.mpq` files onto the page. 3. When the page says **All files found.**, click **ENTER SANCTUARY**. 4. On the main menu, click **SINGLE PLAYER**, pick a hero, type a name and click **OK**. | the main menu | creating a hero | |---|---| | ![The Diablo II: Lord of Destruction main menu, with Single Player, Battle.net and Other Multiplayer buttons](docs/screenshots/title.png) | ![Select Hero Class: the heroes standing around the campfire, the Barbarian selected](docs/screenshots/class-select.png) | *Screenshots are rendered from the player's own game files; the art is Blizzard's.* > [!NOTE] > **Your files never leave your computer.** The page reads them inside your browser; nothing is > uploaded. Next time, click **Use the files from last time** and skip step 2. > [!TIP] > **Any patch level works here.** The page supplies the 1.13c patch data itself, so an > unpatched install, a 1.14 install or a 1.13c install all play the same. Hover over a file on the file screen to see whether it was found. Saves are kept in your browser's storage on that computer. Battle.net is off; Single Player is the way in. ## Option B: Run your own server with Docker The image `ghcr.io/virtastic/d2-web` holds the engine and the web page, and **no game data**. **Step 1.** Install [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) and start it. **Step 2.** Start the server: ```bash docker run -d --name d2-web --restart unless-stopped -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/virtastic/d2-web:latest ``` **Step 3.** Open and continue from [Option A, step 2](#option-a-play-in-your-browser): each player chooses their own game folder in their own browser. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Use HTTPS for anything other than `localhost`.** The engine needs a browser feature > (`SharedArrayBuffer`) that browsers only allow on `https://` or `localhost`. Put HTTPS in front > of the container, for example with Caddy, nginx or a Cloudflare Tunnel.
Serve the game files from the server instead (D2_ASSETS=hosted) By default (`D2_ASSETS=byo`, "bring your own") the server holds no game files and each player picks their own. With `D2_ASSETS=hosted`, the server serves the `.mpq` files from a folder you mount at `/retail`, and players just open the page: ```bash docker run -d --name d2-web --restart unless-stopped -p 8080:8080 \ -e D2_ASSETS=hosted -v "/path/to/Diablo II:/retail:ro" ghcr.io/virtastic/d2-web:latest ``` Or with Compose: ```yaml services: d2-web: image: ghcr.io/virtastic/d2-web:latest restart: unless-stopped ports: ["8080:8080"] environment: D2_ASSETS: hosted # or byo, and drop the volume volumes: ["/path/to/Diablo II:/retail:ro"] ``` > [!WARNING] > Anyone who can open the page can download those files. Use hosted mode only for players who > own the game, for example behind a login such as Cloudflare Access.
## Option C: Build from source You need Linux, macOS, or Windows with WSL2, plus: | tool | why | get it | |---|---|---| | Docker | the engine compiles inside a container, so you do not install a compiler | | | Node.js 24 or newer | runs the setup, the build helpers and the local server | | | git | downloads the code | | | Diablo II + Lord of Destruction, **patched to 1.13c** | used to create the delta patch for users, to ensure they are on 1.13c | your own copy | ### Step 1. Download the code ```sh git clone --recursive https://github.com/Virtastic/d2-web.git cd d2-web ``` `--recursive` also downloads StormLib, the library that reads `.mpq` files. If you forget it, the next step fetches it for you. ### Step 2. Point it at your game ```sh node tools/setup.mjs "/path/to/Diablo II" ``` This one command does all of the game-file setup: - finds your `.mpq` files, whatever their capitalisation; - links them into `retail/D2/`, where the build and the local server look for them, without copying (git ignores that folder, so game files can never be committed); - checks that `patch_d2.mpq` is the 1.13c patch; - checks that Docker is running and that StormLib is present. When everything is in place it prints: ```text d2-web setup Game files from /path/to/Diablo II ✓ patch_d2.mpq The 1.13c patch linked ✓ d2exp.mpq Lord of Destruction linked ✓ d2data.mpq Maps, monsters, items linked ✓ d2char.mpq The heroes linked ... ✓ d2xvideo.mpq Expansion cinematics linked Build tools ✓ Node.js 24.11.0 ✓ Docker 28.5.1 ✓ StormLib third_party/StormLib ✓ Ready to build. Next: bash ci/build.sh D2_RETAIL_DIR=retail/D2 node play/serve.mjs 8920 build-wasm/site then open http://localhost:8920 in Chrome. ``` Fix any line marked **✗**, then run the command again; it is safe to repeat. A line marked **!** is a file the game needs to play but the build can do without. > [!TIP] > **Your patch is not 1.13c?** Setup tells you. Either update the game to 1.13c, or keep your > install as it is and point setup at a 1.13c `Patch_D2.mpq` you have elsewhere: > `node tools/setup.mjs "/path/to/Diablo II" --patch /path/to/1.13c/Patch_D2.mpq` ### Step 3. Build ```sh bash ci/build.sh ``` This builds a compiler image, compiles the engine to WebAssembly and writes the finished site to `build-wasm/site/`. The first run takes a while; later runs reuse what is already built. Near the end, the log prints: ```text patch shim: retail/D2/patch_d2.mpq (8229959 bytes, 1.13c) -> build-wasm/site/assets/patch-113c.patch door-art: ... images -> build-wasm/site/door-art ``` > [!NOTE] > Changed only JavaScript in `play/`? `bash ci/stage.sh` restages the site in seconds without > recompiling the engine. ### Step 4. Play ```sh D2_RETAIL_DIR=retail/D2 node play/serve.mjs 8920 build-wasm/site ``` Open in Chrome. `play/serve.mjs` is a small Node server with no dependencies. It serves the site, serves your `.mpq` files from `D2_RETAIL_DIR`, and sends the cross-origin isolation headers (COOP/COEP) that the engine's threads need. > [!IMPORTANT] > **A plain static file server will not work**: it does not send those headers. Use > `play/serve.mjs` or the Docker image.
What the build takes from your game files, and why The front door (the title screen a player sees before choosing their game files) needs two things that are made from **your** game files every time you build. Neither is ever committed, which is why a fresh clone does not have them. | staged path | what it is | made from | made by | without it | |---|---|---|---|---| | `assets/patch-113c.patch` | your 1.13c `patch_d2.mpq`, as base64 text | `patch_d2.mpq` | `tools/patch-shim.mjs` | **the build stops** | | `door-art/` | the title-screen art, drawn before any files are chosen | `patch_d2.mpq`, `d2exp.mpq`, `d2data.mpq` | `tools/door-art.mjs` | warning; the title screen uses a plain web font until the player's files load | | `freeres/` | the widescreen bottom bar and border panels: 16 `.dc6` files plus their licence | `play/freeres/` in git (SGD2FreeRes art, under its own licence) | `ci/stage.sh` copies it | the build stops | | `widebg/` | optional widescreen menu backgrounds | images you supply | `ci/stage.sh` copies them | the menus use the game's own 4:3 backgrounds | **Why the patch file exists.** Pl

Ratchet & Clank on PC, natively.
The PlayStation 2 games, decompiled back into C and rebuilt for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android.

Play · Progress · Make mods · Help out · Docs

## What is OpenRAC? OpenRAC brings the PlayStation 2 Ratchet & Clank games to PC as real native games. No emulator. - **Playable now:** Ratchet & Clank (PAL / NTSC). - **Playable, not yet tried by players:** Ratchet & Clank's PAL v1.00 and Japanese discs, each built from the same C as PAL v2.00. - **Playable, early and unstable:** Going Commando, from any of its three discs (USA v1.01, USA v2.00 Greatest Hits, Europe's *Locked and Loaded*). The launcher builds it from your disc: on Windows and Android with nothing else to install, on Linux and macOS with a compiler you install. - **In progress:** Up Your Arsenal, Deadlocked, Size Matters and Secret Agent Clank. - **How:** each game is decompiled into C that rebuilds the original exactly, then built for your PC. - **No game files included:** models, textures, sound and levels come from your own disc. ## Play 1. [Download the launcher](https://github.com/OpenRAC/OpenRAC/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open it and pick the folder with your disc images (`.iso` or `.chd`). 3. Press **Play**. The launcher sets your games up for you. Nothing else to install, and no game is ever downloaded. **More:** [Supported discs](baserom/README.md) · [Games and versions](games/README.md) ## Progress How much of each game's code is decompiled so far.
